register.name: First Biennial Transparency Report and Second National Communication
register.detail: GEF Trust Fund · GEF ID 12366 · approved for implementation 18 June 2026 · UNDP, with INCOMA as executing agency · no co-financing
register.note: A grant for climate reporting under the Paris Agreement
register.text: A GEF grant of US$1,233,000, implemented by UNDP, to help Equatorial Guinea prepare its first Biennial Transparency Report and a combined second Biennial Transparency Report and second National Communication. It finances no service directly; it builds national capacity to report on climate action and to bring climate into national development planning.

register.name: Climate Resilience Agrifood Value Chains Project (PADCVA)
register.detail: IFAD · approved 29 December 2025 under the lapse-of-time procedure · loan of €6.045M over 20 years, including 5 years’ grace · eight years · total cost €54.146M
register.note: Planned co-financing in the IFAD report: an Adaptation Fund grant of €17.271M, a BDEAC loan of €8.635M and €12.687M from the government
register.text: An IFAD loan of EUR 6.045 million towards a project of EUR 54.146 million over eight years that builds agrifood value chains able to withstand climate change. It targets 20,000 people directly, 40% of them women and 40% young people, with smallholder producers first. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Staff Monitored Program, third review
register.detail: IMF · Non-financing · Approved by IMF management 16 December 2025
register.note: Non-financing: the programme builds the reform track record for a possible IMF financing arrangement
register.text: Reforms to adjust the economy to structurally lower hydrocarbon output; the IMF estimates a 6.4% contraction in 2025.

register.name: Biodiversity and biocarbon finance instruments for forest conservation
register.detail: GEF Trust Fund · GEF ID 11247 · approved for implementation 7 January 2025 · UNEP, with the Ministry of Forests and Environment, INDEFOR-AP and INCOMA · co-financing $34M
register.note: Economic instruments for carbon and biodiversity, with better livelihoods for Indigenous peoples and local communities
register.text: A GEF grant of US$4,131,301, implemented by UNEP, to develop finance instruments that reward carbon sequestration and biodiversity protection in Equatorial Guinea’s forest landscapes, with US$34 million of co-financing. Its four components cover the enabling environment, methods and capacity, natural capital valuation and incentives, and knowledge and monitoring. It serves the livelihood standard of forest communities and puts a value on the forest.

register.name: Project to Strengthen Human Capital in Support of Economic and Social Inclusion, phase 1 (PARCH 1)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · approval announced 29 September 2025 · signed in Bata 30 October 2025 · 2025–2030 · total cost €73.27M, with €14.65M from the government
register.note: The Bank’s first investment in the country’s human development sectors for ten years
register.text: African Development Bank financing of EUR 58.61 million for a five-year project of EUR 73.27 million that improves vocational training and access to jobs for young people, with two polytechnic institutes in Mongomo and Luba. It aims to train nearly 2,000 young people, 45% of them women, create 4,500 jobs and establish 500 businesses run by young people and women. It serves the education standard, the one furthest from reach, and the livelihood standard.

register.name: Aseng Gas Monetisation Project
register.detail: Chevron (Noble Energy EG), GEPetrol, Glencore and Gunvor · Investment decision 31 March 2026
register.note: GEPetrol’s stake rose from 5% to 32.55% under a February 2026 agreement
register.text: Gas from offshore Block I to domestic power and to the EG LNG plant at Punta Europa, part of the Gas Mega Hub.

register.name: Bioko Island Malaria Elimination Project, national expansion
register.detail: MCD Global Health · five-year agreement announced 14 January 2026 · ConocoPhillips, Chevron, SONAGAS, GEPetrol and the Government of Equatorial Guinea · first extension to the mainland and Annobón
register.note: Malaria prevalence on Bioko fell to 7.2% across all ages in 2025, from 42% in 2004
register.text: A five-year agreement of US$74.4 million, financed by energy companies and the government, that renews the malaria elimination project run on Bioko Island since 2004 and takes it, for the first time, to mainland Equatorial Guinea and Annobón Island. It serves the health standard.
